A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.

terra.problem: The LORD speaks of forming Jacob. The explanation extends that statement to the individual baker without support from the passage.
The claim that the Bible calls the LORD a shepherd elsewhere needs a reference.
The shelf joke risks placing the LORD alongside idols. Humor must not target God.
The sidekick joke makes the LORD the subject of the humor.
A witness can carry a sword. The passage doesn't make that distinction.
The period-versus-maybe punchline makes the way Scripture is written the joke.
The cookie-taster comparison puts down people who couldn't see or understand what they were assessing.
The passage doesn't say idols cannot stand or walk. The blanket claim that they cannot stand is also misleading.
The passage says the blacksmith grows weak, not that he fails to become richer. Those aren't opposites.
The claim about animal-shaped idols elsewhere in the Bible needs a reference.
The claim that the text gives no other reason overlooks verse 20, which says the man's deluded heart has led him astray.
The explanation treats feeding on ashes as a literal diet and adds that the rest of the wood led him to ashes. The text doesn't say that.
The explanation adds that the smoke is gone and ashes are left on the ground, treating the image as a literal scene the text doesn't give.
The verse calls the heavens and mountains to sing and the depths to shout. It doesn't say all three are told to shout or that the whole creation sings.
